name: United States Government (federal AI-related programs)
monetization: Not a profit-seeker by charter, but now a direct financial participant in the AI economy: ~10% equity in Intel, a 15% cut of Nvidia/AMD China chip revenue, profit participation in the Westinghouse nuclear buildout, and $1-a-year AI procurement that shapes lab revenue quality.
description_md: This record tracks the US federal government's financial positions in the AI ecosystem, which since mid-2025 have gone far beyond procurement: equity stakes in strategic suppliers, revenue-share license conditions on chip exports, nuclear-buildout profit participation, and loss-leader AI purchasing across agencies. It is simultaneously the ecosystem's regulator (export controls), customer (DoD/GSA), shareholder (Intel), and — via the Anthropic ban — its most consequential single counterparty risk.
ai_monetization_md: Positions, in order of financial weight: (1) an $8.9B purchase of 433.3M non-voting Intel shares at $20.47 (~9.9%), funded by converting unpaid CHIPS Act grants ($5.7B) and Secure Enclave funding ($3.2B), closed Aug 27, 2025 — a passive stake with no board seat; (2) a license arrangement under which Nvidia and AMD remit 15% of China chip revenue (H20/MI308-class) to the US government as an export-license condition (Aug 2025); (3) the Oct 2025 Westinghouse partnership: the government arranges financing/permitting for ≥$80B of AP1000/AP300 reactors and receives, once vested, 20% of Westinghouse cash distributions above $17.5B; (4) DoD/CDAO contracts of up to $200M each with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI (Jul 2025) — ceilings, not obligations (OpenAI's award had only ~$2M obligated initially); (5) GSA OneGov agreements putting ChatGPT and Claude into agencies at $1/agency/year (Gemini at $0.47) — distribution-buying by the labs, near-zero federal revenue.
risk_notes_md: Policy is the risk channel: the Feb 27, 2026 order for federal agencies to cease using Anthropic products — with DoD designating Anthropic a supply-chain risk (formalized Mar 3, 2026, the first such designation of a US company) after Anthropic refused to waive surveillance/autonomous-weapons restrictions — killed a federal pipeline overnight and demonstrated that US-government AI relationships can reverse without financial process. For counterparties, government ceilings (DoD $200M) and $1 deals are revenue-quality traps: high headline, minimal realized. The Intel stake and 15% China arrangement have no modern legal template and face ongoing challenge risk.

observations.notes: 433.3M non-voting shares at $20.47 (~9.9%); $5.7B converted CHIPS grants + $3.2B Secure Enclave; closed 2025-08-27; part held in escrow pending Secure Enclave disbursements. No board seat.
15% of China H20/MI308 revenue as a license condition; largely moot for new sales after 2026 bans extended to offshore Chinese data centers (Jun 1, 2026).

events.title: DoD awards contracts of up to $200M each to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI
events.why_it_matters: Ceiling ≠ revenue: OpenAI's award had only ~$2M obligated initially — the canonical example of headline-vs-realized in government AI contracting.

events.title: GSA OneGov: ChatGPT and Claude at $1/agency/year, Gemini at $0.47
events.why_it_matters: Labs bought federal distribution at a loss — near-zero revenue now, procurement lock-in later; a protest against the $1 agreements followed within weeks.

events.title: Takes ~10% equity stake in Intel for $8.9B via converted grants
events.why_it_matters: Unprecedented peacetime federal shareholding in a strategic chipmaker; by 2026 the stake's paper value had roughly quadrupled.

events.title: Announces $80B Westinghouse nuclear partnership with profit participation
events.why_it_matters: The state underwrites AI-era power supply and takes upside: 20% of Westinghouse distributions above $17.5B once an $80B reactor program is definitively agreed.

events.title: Federal agencies ordered off Anthropic; DoD designates it a supply-chain risk
events.why_it_matters: The first-ever such designation of a US company (formalized Mar 3, 2026) after Anthropic refused to waive restrictions on mass surveillance and autonomous weapons; agencies got six months to phase out Claude — eliminating Anthropic's federal pipeline and repricing 'government AI revenue' risk for every lab.
